findings.evidence: Measured in frontend/src, non-test .ts/.tsx: hex colours 197 (top files hooks/useChartTheme.ts 55, components/ui/charts/StandardRadarChart.tsx 32, lib/chartColors.ts 27, pdfGenerator.ts 23, config/taxonomy/SkillDomainsSection.tsx 18); rgb(a) numeric literals 76; raw palette classes such as bg-red-500, text-green-600 etc. 415 (lib/designSystem.ts 77, StandardRadarChart.tsx 40, config/communication/CefrDocumentationTab.tsx 39, types/communication.ts 36, types/behavioral.ts 30, ActionableGapsTable.tsx 16, BehavioralPillarsCard.tsx 13, CefrPromotionGatingTab.tsx 13). Part of this is legitimate (chart theme files and the print window in pdfGenerator.ts must use literals), but types/*.ts and designSystem.ts holding palette classes means colours are decided in data types. Theme switching is only reliable where rgb(var(--token)) is used.
findings.impact_text: Dark mode and rebranding will leave some screens with wrong or unreadable colours.
findings.root_cause: Token rule is enforced by review only; no lint rule for palette classes outside the theme files.
findings.fix: Move colours in types/*.ts and designSystem.ts to semantic token classes, route chart literals through one theme file, and add an eslint/CI check that lists new raw colours (allowlist the theme files and pdfGenerator).
findings.test: CI audit count of raw colours outside the allowlist trends to 0.

findings.title: No code splitting: one 931 KB main script plus a 437 KB chart chunk are loaded before the login screen
findings.urgency_reason: One 931 KB script loads before the first screen.
findings.evidence: grep for lazy( / React.lazy in src (non-test) returns nothing, so every screen is imported statically (routes.tsx:2-3 imports LoginPage and DashboardPage directly). The latest dist (dated 2026-09-23, so figures may be slightly out of date) has index-92f26164.js 931,581 bytes, ui-5b5d8462.js 437,612, react-vendor 201,048, query 41,247. vite.config.ts:54-58 manualChunks only separates vendors and lists `tailwindcss` (a build tool, not a runtime library) in the 'ui' chunk; d3 is a dependency (package.json:29) but no import of d3 exists in src (grep). Source maps are off (no build.sourcemap, no .map files in dist), which is good.
findings.impact_text: Login and first dashboard load download more than 1.5 MB of script, slow on office VPN or mobile.
findings.root_cause: Everything is statically imported; chunking is by vendor only.
findings.fix: Wrap Reports, Setup, AI Insights and Bulk Assessment in React.lazy with Suspense, put recharts in its own lazy chunk, remove tailwindcss from manualChunks and the unused d3 dependency.
findings.test: vite build output shows main chunk under 400 KB; Lighthouse JS transfer for /login drops accordingly.

findings.title: Several important backend files are poorly covered (overall 66% lines, below the 80% gate)
findings.urgency_reason: Backend coverage is below the 80% gate.
findings.evidence: From coverage/lcov.info (61 source files, 3585 lines, 2369 covered = 66%): communication.service.ts 26% (74 lines missed), reports.controller.ts 29% (48 missed), ai.service.ts 54% (82 missed), report-data.service.ts 51% (54 missed), communication.controller.ts 50%, behavioral.service.ts 40%, scoring-config.service.ts 45%, config.controller.ts 69% (153 missed), config.service.ts 68% (120 missed). Scripts under src/scripts have 0% (seed/backfill, 4 files) and are not important. coverage/coverage-summary.json is stale (3 files, 2026-09-24) and should not be used.
findings.impact_text: The reporting and CEFR code that drives promotion decisions is the least tested part of the backend.
findings.root_cause: Coverage rule applies to new code only, so older modules were never brought up.
findings.fix: Add tests for communication.service, reports.controller and report-data.service first (they feed promotion readiness), then ai.service fallback path.
findings.test: Per-file coverage >= 80% for those five files in the next lcov.

findings.title: Help modals are missing on all 6 dashboard tabs, all 42 Setup screens and 4 report tabs
findings.urgency_reason: Breaks the help-on-every-screen standard.
findings.evidence: <HelpButton is used in 14 non-test files, all under components/reports (CefrAnalyticsTab, CompetencyScoresTab, DomainScoresTab, ExecutiveLeaderboardTab, ExecutiveSummaryTab, PromotionReadinessTab/Detail, plus shared parts). Zero uses under components/dashboard (tabs: OverviewTab, ResourceOverviewDashboard, TeamHealthCharts, AssessmentsTab, AIInsightsTab, AdminDashboardTab) and zero under components/config (42 .tsx files). Report tabs without it: GapAnalysisTab, StarRatingsTab, YoYGrowthTab, EmployeeResultSheetTab. Only 6 *Help.ts data files exist (all in reports/tabs). Violates the help-on-screens rule (STANDARDS section 5e).
findings.impact_text: Users get no in-app explanation of metrics on the screens they open first, so they ask the owner.
findings.root_cause: Help was added report by report and never extended to dashboard and setup.
findings.fix: Add a *Help.ts per dashboard tab and Setup section and render HelpButton in the shared tile/section header; add a CI check that every tab file imports HelpButton.
findings.test: Unit test or script listing tab components without HelpButton returns empty.

findings.title: Frontend end-to-end tests only prove screens render against a mocked API; no real login-to-approval flow
findings.urgency_reason: End-to-end tests run against a mocked API.
findings.evidence: e2e has 5 specs, 462 lines in total: smoke.spec.ts (login page, dashboard 'renders with an empty API', Setup screens, themes), screens.spec.ts (every top tab/report renders), session-reload.spec.ts (3 reload/new-tab cases), cefr-modal.spec.ts (1), skill-run.spec.ts (2: create skill, empty name refused). harness.ts:52-57 intercepts every `**/api/v1/**` request with page.route and fulfills 200 JSON; login is also faked (line 70). No spec uses a real backend, no assessment-to-approval-to-report path, no role-restricted behaviour. Positive: 0 skipped or disabled tests found in e2e or src (grep test.skip/it.skip/xdescribe/fixme), and 2,334 unit tests pass.
findings.impact_text: A break between frontend and backend (field rename, permission change) is found by users, not by the test run.
findings.root_cause: e2e was added as a render-crash safety net, not as an integration suite.
findings.fix: Add 3 contract-style flows against a seeded test backend in CI: engineer saves a skill, line manager approves, report shows the result; plus one 403 check per restricted tab.
findings.test: The new flows in CI on every master push.

chains.title: A leaked hash becomes a lasting account takeover
steps: An admin or any caller of the assignment endpoints reads password hashes from API responses.
The same hashes are stored in the audit log and persist.
Login lockout and username leaks help an attacker pick targets.
A password reset does not end existing sessions.

chains.title: Approvals can be bypassed and nobody can tell
steps: Any manager can set a CEFR result for anyone.
An engineer can change an approved skill through the create route.
User and role changes are not logged.

chains.title: Scores can be wrong or lost without any signal
steps: A recompute error is swallowed after the assessment is saved.
Two simultaneous saves can overwrite each other.

chains.title: A bad release reaches production with no way back
steps: A stale main branch can publish production images.
Deploys default to the moving latest tag.
Production migrations run with no backup step.
Backups sit unprotected with no retention.

waves.name: Stop the exposure
waves.goal: Contain credential exposure and close the CEFR approval hole.
exit_criteria: Hashes cannot appear in any API response or new audit-log row (HTTP tests prove it).
A manager cannot change a CEFR result outside their scope (test).
The owner has scrubbed existing audit-log rows and rotated affected passwords (done by hand).
The owner has confirmed whether the demo logins exist in production, and removed them from the build.
waves.why_order: These four are U0: active exposure or a one-line fix. Everything else depends on trusting these basics.

waves.name: Trust the pipeline and the tests
waves.goal: Make delivery safe and add the HTTP role tests every later fix needs.
exit_criteria: Only master publishes production images, and images are pinned by version.
An HTTP role-by-route test runs in CI against the real route chain.
The pipeline runs a dependency and image scan; npm audit --omit=dev shows no high or critical on backend.
waves.why_order: The tests and the pipeline are prerequisites: access and history fixes need them to be provable and safe to ship.

waves.name: Access control and sessions
waves.goal: Close the remaining approval, session and audit-trail gaps.
exit_criteria: An approved skill cannot change without re-approval (test).
Logout and password change end refresh tokens (test).
User, role and password changes appear in the audit log.
Self-approval policy for senior roles is decided (D1) and enforced.
waves.why_order: These changes alter who can do what, so they follow the role tests from W1.

waves.name: Make scores trustworthy
waves.goal: Make the assessment write atomic and remove invented or duplicated numbers.
exit_criteria: Assessment write and score recompute succeed or fail together (test).
No screen shows an invented width or a recomputed readiness rule.
Absent data shows as absent, never as zero.
waves.why_order: Atomicity must exist before the history change (W4). The data-truth fixes are small and visible.

waves.name: Appraisal history
waves.goal: Keep results per period and make locked periods and scoring config truly immutable.
exit_criteria: Re-assessing in period 2 leaves period 1 untouched (test).
A locked period cannot be changed even by direct database writes.
Editing weights does not change a locked period's results (test).
Migration proven on a local disposable database with before/after counts.
waves.why_order: Highest fix risk and a data migration: it goes after tests and the atomic write, and starts with a plan you approve.

waves.name: Platform hardening
waves.goal: Harden containers, headers, backups, errors and the AI integration.
exit_criteria: Both images run as non-root on pinned bases.
CSP and security headers are in place; port 4000 is not public.
Backups are protected and have retention.
Errors returned to clients carry no internal detail.
waves.why_order: Real but not urgent; can be done in parallel by a second person once W1 is in.

waves.name: UI quality and maintainability
waves.goal: Fix dialog accessibility, help coverage, routing and the largest files.
exit_criteria: Confirm dialog ignores stray Enter; focus is trapped and restored.
Every screen has its Help button.
Initial JavaScript is split.
waves.why_order: Lowest exposure. The routing decision (D5) may change the scope, so it comes last.

decisions.question: Do the five demo logins (one per role, including an Admin; see DemoAccounts.tsx lines 7 to 11) exist in production with the shared test password? Only you can check.
options: Yes: change those passwords and remove the demo list from the build.
No: remove the demo list from the build anyway.
decisions.recommended: Check production now; remove the list from production builds either way.

decisions.question: Who approves the self-assessments of ADMIN and TOP_MANAGEMENT users?
options: They may self-approve, but it is logged and reported.
decisions.recommended: Four-eyes: another admin or top manager approves.

decisions.question: Which registry replaces the personal Docker Hub namespace for production images?
decisions.recommended: A company-owned registry that your CI already authenticates to.

decisions.question: How should database backups be stored, encrypted and retained?
options: Encrypted object storage with 30 day retention
Encrypted VM disk with 14 day retention
decisions.recommended: Encrypted, off-host, with a tested restore and a stated retention period.

decisions.question: Which rule defines "ready" on screen?
options: The backend field (promotion_ready / meetsAllChecks) everywhere; screens never recompute.
decisions.recommended: The backend field, as your metric rules already say.

decisions.question: Should the app get real URLs per screen (deep links, Back button)?
options: Yes: one route per tab and Setup section.
No: keep the single-page tab model.
decisions.recommended: Yes, in a later wave; it also simplifies access checks.

decisions.question: For appraisal history: should a new period start with a copy of the last period's assessments, and how many periods are kept?
options: Copy forward and keep all periods.
decisions.recommended: Copy forward and keep all periods; show the migration plan first.

strengths.title: Access token is re-validated against the database on every request
strengths.detail: authenticate() verifies the JWT, then loads the user and rejects inactive users, and takes role and employee id from the database, not from the token. A deactivated or re-roled user is cut off within one request. Access token lifetime is 15 minutes.

strengths.title: Refresh token is stored hashed, lives in an httpOnly strict cookie, and is not returned in the body
strengths.detail: Refresh tokens are SHA-256 hashed in refresh_tokens, cookie has httpOnly, sameSite strict, secure in production; the access token is held in memory only (Zustand, no localStorage), and the session flag in sessionStorage holds no secret. Refresh checks signature, stored hash, revoked flag, expiry and user is_active.

strengths.title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt cost 12 and the login response carries no hash
strengths.detail: bcryptjs with cost 12 for create, update and change-password; login and /auth/me return an explicit field list, not the user row. JWT secrets must be at least 32 characters (env schema).

strengths.title: CORS is a single configured origin and helmet is enabled with HSTS
strengths.detail: cors uses env.FRONTEND_URL (no wildcard) with credentials, explicit methods and headers; helmet is on with a CSP and a one-year HSTS. nginx also sets HSTS, nosniff, frame deny and referrer policy, and rate limits login by real remote address.

strengths.title: Login has app-level and edge rate limiting plus account lockout
strengths.detail: express-rate-limit 10 per minute on /auth/login, nginx limit_req on login keyed by $binary_remote_addr, and 5-failure account lock. (See findings for the proxy and lockout gaps.)

strengths.title: Technical skill write routes are scope-checked per object and strip engineer-set levels
strengths.detail: create, update, delete, approve, submit-drafts and read all resolve the target employee and call canAccessEmployee with forAssessment; ENGINEER and managers on their own record cannot set level and get draft status on update; approve refuses LM/MANAGER on their own record with 403 SELF_APPROVAL_PROHIBITED. Pending queue excludes the manager's own rows.

strengths.title: Mass assignment is prevented by Zod schemas that strip unknown keys
strengths.detail: Assessment, CEFR, behavioral and user schemas are plain z.object (not passthrough) and the validated data replaces req.body; services build prisma data from named fields, not spread of the body. updateRole is the one with passthrough only on config policy (admin only).

strengths.title: Behavioral and CEFR read paths and CEFR create are scope-checked; improvement plans block self-authoring
strengths.detail: Behavioral reads return 404 for out-of-scope ids so ids cannot be probed; CEFR create, latest, history and expectation call canAccessEmployee; CEFR create demotes LM/MANAGER self-assessment to pending; improvement plans refuse self-authoring and check forAssessment scope.

strengths.title: Role hierarchy permission codes match between backend and frontend
strengths.detail: PERMISSION_CODES (11 codes) are identical in backend/src/types/rbac.ts and frontend/src/types/rbac.ts. The only difference is the two extra frontend roles, which is the accepted mapping. Permissions are looked up from the database (role_permissions) on each requirePermission call and a deactivated role passes nothing.

strengths.title: Config and admin routes all use requirePermission or requireRole
strengths.detail: All 86 routes in config.router.ts are behind authenticate plus requirePermission, requirePermissionOrRole or requireRole; every write is permission-gated and validate(schema) is present on every POST/PUT/PATCH.

strengths.title: Scoring stores a per-assessment score snapshot
strengths.detail: skill_assessments.score is stored at write time and preferred by computeCompetencyScore, so old weights do not rewrite existing assessment rows (except zero scores).

strengths.title: Login and refresh path uses bcrypt cost 12 and a login rate limiter
strengths.detail: Passwords hashed with bcryptjs cost 12; express-rate-limit on login.

strengths.title: Validation on every config write route
strengths.detail: All post/put/patch routes in config.router.ts use validate(zod schema), with parsed data replacing req.body.

strengths.title: AI has deterministic fallback and bounded inputs
strengths.detail: Failures fall back to a deterministic answer; question clamped to 600 chars; focus allow-listed; output coerced to a fixed shape.

strengths.title: Multi-step config writes use transactions with audit rows
strengths.detail: createEmployee and line-manager flows use db.$transaction with tx.accessAuditLog.

strengths.title: DB-level guard on CEFR scale
strengths.detail: Trigger cefr_levels_scale_lock protects the scale in the database.

strengths.title: Security headers, CORS pinned, body limit
strengths.detail: helmet with HSTS, CORS restricted to FRONTEND_URL, 1mb JSON limit.

strengths.title: Tokens are not stored in the browser; a reload restores the session from an httpOnly cookie
strengths.detail: authStore keeps the access token in memory only (no persist, no localStorage); sessionStorage holds only a flag with no token, and lib/session.ts restores via the refresh cookie. Refresh requests are de-duplicated and a failed refresh clears state and the query cache. Access is also checked on the server; tab guards in the UI are display only.

strengths.title: The one XSS-prone sink is escaped
strengths.detail: The only window.open / document.write is the result-sheet print window; every data value in its HTML goes through esc() (employee name, code, department, domains, competencies). No dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML anywhere in src. Source maps are not shipped.

strengths.title: CI order is safe: scan, quality gate, Sonar gate, then image build
strengths.detail: Both pipelines run gitleaks, lint, type-check, tests with coverage, build, Sonar with qualitygate.wait before any docker push. The frontend also runs check:css and the project's own defect-class audit. Login uses --password-stdin. Dated and short-sha tags are pushed for every production image.

strengths.title: Cache headers and API proxy in the frontend nginx are well thought out
strengths.detail: index.html is no-store, /assets/ is immutable for a year, unhashed files revalidate; nginx/nginx.conf has TLS 1.2+, HSTS, a 10 req/min login limit zone and a 1 MB body cap.

strengths.title: Backups and restores avoid hard-coded secrets and verify integrity
strengths.detail: backup and restore scripts use an AWS profile, a SHA-256 checksum uploaded beside the dump, set -euo pipefail and clear failure messages. No curl-to-shell or chmod 777 in the scripts. Deploy scripts pin tags by argument and run prisma migrate deploy (not db push).

strengths.title: Clean test hygiene
strengths.detail: No skipped or disabled tests in frontend src, e2e or backend src (0 matches for skip/fixme/xdescribe/it.todo). Frontend has 136 test files; vitest is configured with all:true so untested files count in coverage. Playwright specs are kept out of vitest.

strengths.title: Data-truth rules are mostly followed in the frontend
strengths.detail: Math.random is used only for row/toast keys, not figures. Only 6 numeric fallbacks (`?? n` / `|| n`) exist outside tests and only one (AIInsightsTab:984) is a display fallback. CSV export uses emp_code. Keyboard: 0 clickable divs without role or key handler. Modal has role=dialog and Escape.

strengths.title: Dev compose does not publish the API port
strengths.detail: deployments/docker-compose.dev.yml uses expose instead of ports for the API, and image healthchecks exist in both Dockerfiles (Node fetch, wget).
